Effects Database groups Audio Designs Fuzzound with Applied's Kimberly/Volume Expander family. The relationship is retained as a research candidate because direct period factory documentation is limited.
Effects Database groups Apollo No. 843 with the later UMI production branch of the Kimberly design family, distinct from the earlier Applied stage.
Effects Database groups Conrad Buzz Box & Volume Expander with the later UMI branch; Conrad is retained as a marketed identity, not treated as the physical builder.

Effects Database describes the UMI Buzz Tone & Volume Expander as a later closely related design descended from earlier Kimberly and Applied Electronics models, with continuity of the two-stage fuzz/boost concept.

Tone Machines states Banshee Fuzz units were sold under Nomad and Applied brands but cautions that manufacturing dates are unknown; Nomad was a LIMMCO house brand. The exact start date is not inherited from the 1968 date of the LIMMCO relationship without model-specific evidence.

Tone Machines identifies the Rogue Fuzz as made by Applied Audio and places it in the later Nomad effects sequence after Banshee; LIMMCO is treated as the distribution/house-brand connection rather than the factory.

Tone Machines and Effects Database treat the Nomad Super Fuzz as a possible mid-1960s Mosrite Fuzzrite-related OEM, while explicitly noting that the Nomad relationship to Mosrite remains unresolved. It must stay separate from later Applied Nomad products.

Tone Machines identifies Nomad as a LIMMCO house brand and describes LIMMCO as the distributor connecting Nomad with Applied Audio; LIMMCO is not promoted as the physical builder of the later Applied Nomad fuzzes.
